sentences.text:
D. Praveen, Armoor Mandal, Nizamabad ... vs A.P. Raod
Transport Corporation And ... on 21 June, 2023

Author: Lalitha Kanneganti
Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2781 of 2008
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the award dated 21.02.2008 in O.P.No.1633 of 2004 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (III Additional District Judge) (FTC), Nizamabad the claimant has filed MACMA No.2781 of 2008.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (III Additional District Judge) (FTC), Nizamabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Having heard learned counsel for appellant-claimant Mr. Radeive Reddy and learned counsel for RTC, perused the entire material on record.
3. The claim petition was filed under Section 166 of M.V Act, seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the claimant in Motor accident by the RTC bus.

It is the case of the petitioner that on 29.10.2004 the petitioner was travelling in the RTC bus from Nizamabad to Armoor and at about 9.00 p.m when it reached Ramchandrapally village sivar, the driver of the bus drove it in a rash and negligent manner and at high speed and dashed against the tipper which was parked by the side of the road due to which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries such as fractures and immediately he was shifted to Govt. Headquarters hospital,
Nizamabad took LK, J MACMA_2781_2008 treatment and after shifted to Gandhi Hospital,
Secunderabad underwent operations and fixed with the implant and after discharge took treatment privately.
According to the claimant, he has sustained fracture of left leg bones, injury of politeal artery left leg and two other grievous injuries.

He submitted that he spent lot of amount for the treatment, the Court below for the two grievous injuries granted Rs.25,000/- and Rs.15,000/- i.e.,
Rs.40,000/- for two grievous injuries and Rs.33,000/- for the treatment and medicines.

Coming to loss of income, it is the case of the claimants that he is earning Rs.10,000/- doing agriculture and business, the Court below has considered Rs.100/- and granted Rs.15,000/- to loss of income for five (5) months, because of the injuries he could not work.
The Doctor has deposed that he has suffered 35 % of disability that was not considered by the Court and accordingly, granted an amount of Rs.92,000/-.

4. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company filed counter denying the manner of accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle and the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant and the amount that was spent by LK, J MACMA_2781_2008 him for his treatment.
It is stated that the claim is excessive and exorbitant.

entities.text: D. Praveen, Armoor Mandal, Nizamabad ... vs A.P. Raod Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Court below on analyzing the oral and documentary evidence has granted compensation of Rs.92,000/- with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant-claimant submits that the amounts that were granted by the Tribunal were not reasonable, he has sustained two grievous injuries and was not operated, he has spent huge amounts and also taken Rs.3000/- as income that he is earning Rs.10,000/- per month.

He further submits that the said findings of the Court below are contrary to the evidence of record.
5.
Learned counsel appearing for RTC submits that the Court below considering the evidence has granted compensation which is just and reasonable.

In this case the claimant has sustained two grievous injuries which was operated, though the Doctor has given the evidence that he has sustained 35 % disability, the evidence of the Doctor is not supported by any LK, J MACMA_2781_2008 certificate issued by the board, the evidence of the Doctor is not based on any of the parameters, hence the Court below has rightly have not considered the disability.
6. Coming to the injuries as per the two grievous injuries he has entitled for Rs.40,000/- each injury i.e., (Rs.40,000 X 2) = 80,000/- for the loss of income.

He claimed Rs.10,000/-, the Court has granted Rs.10,000/-, this Court is inclined to take Rs.4,500 and it was observed that he failed to work for five months, the loss of income comes to Rs.22,500/- (Rs.4,500 X 5).

For the treatment, the Court below has granted Rs.33,000/- which is based on the perusal of the evidence and this Court is inclined to grant Rs.10,000/- for extra nourishment, for transport Rs.10,000/-, for the injuries sustained and towards pain and suffering Rs.20,000/-, towards attendant Rs.10,000/-, altogether the claimant is entitled for Rs.1,85,500/-.

6. In the light of the above discussion, the claimant is entitled for the following compensation under different heads:
LK, J MACMA_2781_2008 Head Compensation awarded (1) Two grievous injury Rs.80,000 (Rs.40,000 X 2) (2) Loss of Income Rs.22,500 (Rs.4,500 X 5) (3)
Treatment Rs.33,000/-
 (4) Pain and Suffering Rs.20,000  (5) Attendant Rs.10,000  (6) Extra Nourishment Rs.10,000  (7) Transport Rs.10,000

Total compensation awarded Rs.1,85,500/-
7.
In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is allowed by enhancing the compensation amount of Rs.1,85,500/-.

(b) The claimant shall pay the Court Fee on the enhanced compensation.
(c) The respondent-insurance company shall deposit the compensation within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt LK, J MACMA_2781_2008 of a copy of this judgment.
On such deposit and on payment of Court fee, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the compensation without furnishing any security.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending in this appeal shall stand dismissed.
